page: Microsoft Azure E96s_v6 is an x86_64 memory-optimized virtual machine powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8573C processor. It features 96 vCPUs mapped to 48 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The processor includes 260 MB of L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for accelerated vector and matrix operations. The instance is equipped with 768.0 GB of RAM, yielding a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, relying instead on external Premium Storage.

In benchmark evaluations, the E96s_v6 demonstrates exceptional memory and multi-core processing capabilities. Memory bandwidth tests place the instance in the top 10% tier, achieving read-only cached speeds of 7,372.61 GB/sec and uncached large-block read speeds of 509.22 GB/sec. Multi-core performance is similarly robust, with top-tier results in PassMark CPU tests and Geekbench multi-core suites. The hardware's AMX and AVX-512 capabilities contribute to strong performance in specialized tasks, including large-model (70B) LLM prompt processing at 41.06 tokens/sec and high-throughput database operations.

From a resource density perspective, the E96s_v6 offers high qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound enterprise workloads by consolidating large databases and memory-intensive applications onto a single high-capacity node. The lack of local storage requires external storage attachment, which represents a configuration tradeoff to consider for IOPS-heavy workloads. This server type is highly suited for large-scale relational databases, in-memory data stores like Redis (which achieved 137.56 million operations per second in testing), high-throughput web serving, and memory-intensive enterprise applications.
